transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… what finally scared me enough to come in is I keep having this thought that it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t tried to hurt myself or anything like that. It’s just been sitting with me, and then I’ll get distracted thinking about the house or some silly thing I forgot at the store, but it comes back, and… well, it scared me.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up?
About four months, I think. It kind of started after my aunt came to live with us… well, around then. Time gets funny for me, but yes, about four months.
Have you been enjoying things you usually like to do over the past four months?

Not really, no. I used to look forward to my watercolors, and there was this dance class I’d go to—well, I wasn’t very good, but the music was nice—and I’d walk with the ladies sometimes. Lately I just… leave my paints sitting there, don’t go, don’t call anybody. I look at it all and I can’t make myself care.
Do you still find pleasure in the things you're doing, even if it's just a little bit?

Maybe a tiny bit here and there, but mostly no. I’ll pick up my paints and just stare at them, or think I should go to dance class, and then I don’t. Even walking with the ladies… I used to like hearing everybody talk about their gardens and grandkids and all that, and now it just feels like too much trouble. I can’t seem to make myself care about it.
Do you often feel guilty about things?

Yes… I do. Mostly with my aunt. If I get tired, or I feel annoyed with her, then I start thinking, what kind of woman am I? She’s family, and I should be grateful I can help, you know… My mother used to say family is everything, and I keep hearing that in my head. Then I feel like I’m bringing shame on everybody because I’m not better about it.
Have you noticed any changes in how active or energetic you are compared to how you used to be?

Yes… I’m a lot more worn out than I used to be. Even if I’ve been in bed all night, I get up and my body feels tired already. Just making breakfast, or carrying a basket of laundry, it feels like more than it ought to. I used to do those things without thinking, you know… now I start one thing and then I have to sit down.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

I don’t know… sleep is kind of hard to explain. Some nights I’m in bed, but I couldn’t tell you if I really slept much or just lay there thinking. And then other times I wake up and the clock is there, and I start remembering I need to wash my aunt’s towels, and then I’m thinking about the old house we used to live in… I’m not sure if that counts as trouble sleeping.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

I’m not really sure… I don’t keep track like that. My clothes maybe feel the same, I think. I haven’t been weighing myself. We used to have a scale in the bathroom, but it got put away somewhere when we moved things around, and then I was looking for towels instead… so I don’t know.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to, or do you feel restless and fidgety?

I guess… yes, maybe slower. My husband keeps saying I move like everything takes extra effort now, like I’m dragging myself through the day. Even at the market, I’ll stand there in the aisle too long before I pick up the thing I came for. Then I start looking at the labels, or remembering we used to buy a different brand years ago… and he’ll say, “Come on, just get it.” So… yes, slower, I think.
Do you ever feel so restless that you can't sit still?

Not really like I can’t sit still… it’s more the opposite, I think. My husband says I move like everything takes extra effort now. Like even at the market, I’ll just stand there too long before I pick up what I came for… and then I get thinking about which one we used to buy, or if my aunt liked that brand, and he’s waiting on me. So no, not restless so much. More slow, I guess.
Do you often feel worthless?

Sometimes, yes. I don’t know if “worthless” is the word, but… when I get tired or annoyed with my aunt, I feel terrible after. I start thinking I’m a bad woman, like I should be more grateful and patient. My family always cared so much about not bringing shame, you know, and then I think maybe I am bringing shame on them by being like this.
Have you been having thoughts about death in general, not just about yourself?

Yes… I mean, I think about it more than I used to. Not like I’ve done anything to hurt myself. I haven’t. It’s more… what scared me enough to come here is I keep thinking maybe it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up.

And then I feel bad even saying that, because my aunt used to say you shouldn’t talk that way, that words can bring trouble… but it’s been in my head. More like death in general, I guess.
Do you ever feel like you're fidgeting or can't stay still when you're sitting or lying down?

No… not fidgeting so much. I’m not tapping my foot or feeling like I have to jump up. It’s more like my body got heavy. My husband says I move like everything takes extra effort now.

Like at the market, I’ll just stand there in front of the shelf too long before I even pick up what I came for… and then I start thinking about whether we used to buy that one, or if my aunt preferred the other one, and people are reaching around me. So, no, I don’t think I can’t stay still. It’s more that I’m too slow.
Do you feel like you're fidgeting or having trouble staying still when you're not feeling slow?

Not really fidgeting, no. It’s more the other way… like I get stuck. My husband says I move like everything takes extra effort now. Even at the market I’ll stand there too long before I pick up what I came for, and then I feel like people are waiting on me, you know. I don’t feel like I can’t stay still so much as I just… slow down.
Do you ever feel like you're fidgeting when you're by yourself?

By myself? No, I don’t think I’m fidgety then either. I mostly just… sit there too long, or move slow. My husband’s the one who notices it most—he says everything looks like it takes extra effort for me now. Even at the market, I’ll stand in front of something too long before I pick it up… then I get to thinking about other things and lose track. So not fidgeting, really. More slowed down.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past four months?

I don’t know… I haven’t really kept track on a scale. My clothes, I mean, some days they feel different, but then laundry shrinks things too, and my sister used to say you can’t trust those old bathroom scales anyway. Four months… that’s a long stretch to remember. I don’t think I’ve noticed some big amount, but I’m not sure.
Have you noticed your clothes fitting looser than they used to?

I haven’t really noticed them being looser, no. I mean, I wear a lot of the same things around the house, and some of them have always been stretched out anyway. My blue pants fit different depending on whether I washed them, and my sister used to say dryers ruin everything. So… I don’t think so, not that I can tell.
Have you lost a noticeable amount of weight recently?

I really can’t say that I have. I mean, I don’t go checking the scale much, and half the time I forget if something fit that way before or if it’s just the wash. My mother used to hang everything on the line so it wouldn’t shrink, and I still think about that when clothes feel odd. But no… I haven’t noticed a clear amount of weight coming off.
Have you had anyone comment on your weight loss recently?

No… I don’t think anyone’s said anything like that. I mean, people don’t really look at me that closely, I suppose, and folks can be funny about commenting on a woman’s weight anyway. My aunt used to do that at every family gathering, just say whatever came into her head. But recently… no, I can’t remember anybody telling me I looked like I lost weight.
Have you lost more than 5% of your body weight over the past four months?

I don’t really know how to figure that, the 5 percent thing. I haven’t been weighing myself regular. We had a scale once that always seemed off, and I stopped trusting those things… my neighbor had one with the little dial and it would stick. So, no, I can’t say I know that I lost that much.
